nodes.label: WS analyst broadcast
nodes.rationale: Monitor broadcasts analysis/report/stats messages on WS /ws, kept separate from events and not stored as events.

nodes.label: st-net internal network
nodes.rationale: app and honeypot only expose internal ports and are reachable exclusively over st-net; only gateway (:8080) and monitor (:9000) publish ports.

nodes.label: File-integrity / tamper monitoring
nodes.rationale: Deferred: matters most for the long-running shell honeypot and multi-host deployment; out of scope for the single-host demo where the gateway is the only writer of each DB.

nodes.label: Rolling hash chain
nodes.rationale: Each record hashes the previous so deletion or in-place edits of historical entries are detectable; a detected gap emits a channel=system tamper event.

nodes.label: App (real vulnerable demo)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately vulnerable (SQLi via string concat in app/db.py, injectable system prompt in app/main.py), fake data only, reachable only through the gateway, never publishes a port.

nodes.label: Ban store (memory)
nodes.rationale: Banned-attacker store persisted in reputation.db; survives restarts and gives instant 403 on return even with cleared cookies (same IP).

nodes.label: Canary token
nodes.rationale: Fake api_keys/secrets embedded in honeypot data; reuse of a canary token triggers canary_hit (risk 10) and an instant ban within a session.

nodes.label: LLM circuit breaker
nodes.rationale: 10s timeout + one retry per call; after 3 consecutive failures pauses calls 30s and the offline analyst takes over, so a flaky tunnel never stalls the demo.

nodes.label: Gateway
nodes.rationale: The only public entry point (:8080). All allow/block/route decisions are 100% deterministic (rules + ban store) and the LLM is never in the attacker's request path, so defense stays fast and safe.

nodes.label: Honeypot
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the real app but serves canaried fake data so the attacker thinks the attack worked; must look identical to the real app to the attacker.

nodes.label: Learning loop / orchestrator
nodes.rationale: When a trapped session ends, the analyst proposes a generalized rule; the headline variant is a paraphrased prompt injection (built-in score 0) to make the strongest before/after story.

nodes.label: Async LLM analyst
nodes.rationale: OpenAI-compatible LLM that narrates attacker actions, writes session reports, and proposes rules; it only analyzes and proposes, never decides allow/block and is never in the request path.

nodes.label: llm_config.json live config
nodes.rationale: Lives on the shared volume, not only env, because a free Kaggle tunnel URL changes every notebook restart and can be updated from the dashboard with no container restart.

nodes.label: Mark as safe (self-correction)
nodes.rationale: Operator override for false positives: disables the over-eager rule and whitelists the payload so the request passes to the real app on retry.

nodes.label: Monitor
nodes.rationale: Stores events, broadcasts over WebSocket to the dashboard, and runs the async LLM analyst + learning orchestrator off the request path.

nodes.label: Offline analyst
nodes.rationale: Built-in fallback so the whole demo works fully offline with the LLM disabled; takes over when the circuit breaker pauses LLM calls.

nodes.label: Deterministic rule engine
nodes.rationale: Built-in SQLi + prompt-injection signatures plus hot-reloaded learned rules; the sole source of flag decisions alongside the ban store.

nodes.label: Shared data volume
nodes.rationale: ./data holds reputation.db, rules.json, events.db, llm_config.json; SQLite uses journal_mode=DELETE because WAL is unreliable on Windows/Docker-Desktop bind mounts, and each DB has exactly one writer service.

nodes.label: Rule validator
nodes.rationale: gateway/validator.py gate: a learned regex must compile, avoid catastrophic backtracking, match the attack, and not match a 70-entry benign corpus before activation — the automated stand-in for human review.

nodes.label: Fake SSH shell honeypot
nodes.rationale: Deferred: needs a longer-lived host and isolated network segment to be safe and believable; the web + prompt honeypot already proves the end-to-end story.

nodes.label: Event contract schema
nodes.rationale: Every service POSTs JSON events to the monitor fire-and-forget; the gateway buffers up to 500 events if the monitor is down; receivers must ignore unknown fields.

nodes.label: Deterministic decision principle
nodes.rationale: Allow/block/route decisions come only from rules + the ban store, never from the LLM and never while waiting on the LLM in the attacker's request path.

nodes.label: LLM output untrusted principle
nodes.rationale: LLM output is JSON-only, validated, and never executed; learned regexes must pass gateway/validator.py before activation.

nodes.label: X-Forwarded-For identity
nodes.rationale: On Docker Desktop all host traffic shares one NAT IP, so demo scripts send fixed demo IPs via XFF (TRUST_XFF=true) to give attackers distinct identities; must be disabled on any real public deployment because it lets clients spoof their IP.
